author: DPA
title: US military completes latest wave of strikes on Iran - NewsBreak
text:
2 hours ago
FILE PHOTO - A satellite image captured by Copernicus Sentinel-3A and provided by ESA shows the Strait of Hormuz, which connects the Gulf of Oman with the Persian Gulf and separates Iran from the countries of the Arabian Peninsula. (is associated with: «US launches fresh strikes on Iran after attempted attack on US forces») -/ESA/dpa The US military said it had successfully concluded a wave of strikes against targets in Iran overnight, describing the attacks as a "powerful" response to attempted Iranian missile attacks on US forces in the Middle East a day earlier.
The strikes targeted military command centres, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defence sites, and maritime capabilities, US Central Command (CENTCOM) said in a post on X after the operation concluded in the early hours of Thursday local time in Iran.
The overnight attacks were aimed at further reducing "threats posed by Iran and its proxies to American forces, commercial shipping, and neighboring Gulf countries", CENTCOM said.
Iranian media earlier reported explosions in the south of the country. The Fars news agency, which is close to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), reported attacks on Qeshm island in the Strait of Hormuz and in Bushehr province.
The US military said Tehran had launched several ballistic missiles at US forces in the Middle East early on Wednesday, local time in Iran, marking Tehran's first reported attack since Washington paused its strikes on Iranian targets over the weekend.
All the missiles were intercepted, according to CENTCOM, which did not specify the intended targets.
Iran's state broadcaster, citing a statement from the IRGC, said the missiles had targeted a US military base in Jordan. Jordan's armed forces said they intercepted five missiles launched from Iran.
Shortly after, US forces and their ally Saudi Arabia also carried out strikes in Iraq against what the US military described as Iran-backed "terrorists." CENTCOM said the strikes were carried out in response to more than 30 drone attacks over the previous 72 hours that it said had been directed by the IRGC.
The United States and Israel began airstrikes on Iran on February 28. Washington and Tehran agreed on a framework in mid-June aimed at ending the conflict through expanded negotiations, but the effort has since unravelled.
A ceasefire that had been in place since April also collapsed after Trump declared it over following what he described as repeated violations. Iran has likewise said it no longer considers itself bound by the arrangement.
